title: Meta Goes Open, OpenAI Arms Cyber Researchers, and Anthropic Holds the Line on Price
tldr: Meta released a free, open-weight model (Muse Glimmer) alongside a Zuckerberg manifesto arguing against AI power concentration — a real build-vs-buy signal.
OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cyber program with GPT-5.6-Cyber; starting September 1, users need physical security keys plus vetting.
Anthropic made Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent rather than raising it as planned this month.

tips.heading: Set up a scheduled AI briefing that only flags real changes
steps: Pick a topic to monitor and the sources it should check.
Give ChatGPT's Scheduled Tasks the prompt below, filling in your topic, sources, and what counts as a meaningful change.
It stays quiet unless something meaningfully shifted — set an end condition so it doesn't run forever.
tips.prompt: Every weekday at 8:00 AM, check [TOPIC] using [SOURCE LIST]. Compare the findings with previous runs. Notify me only if [DEFINITION OF MEANINGFUL CHANGE]. Include the source link, publication time, what changed, and the action I should consider. If nothing qualifies, reply: "No meaningful change." Stop this task after [END CONDITION].

tips.heading: Turn a one-line idea into a live website with ChatGPT and Codex
steps: Plan the build in Astro.js, then have ChatGPT draft a one-page PRD from your idea.
Hand the PRD to Codex (built on GPT-5.6) with sub-agents to build the site.
Iterate on the live preview, then publish through OpenAI's "Sites" skill if you want it hosted for you.

news.body: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a free, open-weight model built for on-device coding and agent workflows — a quantized version reportedly runs on one consumer GPU with ~18GB of memory. Zuckerberg paired it with a 6,500-word manifesto against AI power concentration, proposing broad free access and a $1B fund for communities hosting Meta data centers.
news.means: A real signal in the build-vs-buy debate — an open-weight model good enough for local coding/agent workloads changes the calculus against API-based vendors.

news.body: OpenAI expanded its Daybreak program with GPT-5.6-Cyber, a hacking-tuned model that answers 95% of advanced cyberattack requests the standard GPT-5.6 Sol refuses (vs. 1.5%). Starting September 1, individual users need physical security keys plus vetting and signed authorization.
news.means: A preview of how AI vendors will gate high-risk capabilities — useful if a client's security team asks how vendors manage dual-use risk.

news.body: Anthropic made Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent — $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens — rather than raising it as planned this month.
news.means: Directly useful for cost planning on any Claude-based product or client engagement — a price increase you may have been budgeting for isn't coming.

beyond_ai.body: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, killing at least 111 people and damaging more than 1,500 homes, 50 schools, and 18 health centers near San José del Palmar, Chocó — the country's strongest quake this century, felt as far as Ecuador and Panama.
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: Did you see the scale of the Colombia earthquake — 111 dead and over 1,500 homes damaged? Puts a lot of our "urgent" client fires in perspective.

beyond_ai.body: US markets dipped Monday (S&P -0.1%, Dow -0.1%, Nasdaq -0.3%) as Intel moved to raise $15B in common stock and the US emergency oil reserve fell below 300 million barrels — its lowest level since 1983 — amid supply pressure from the Iran conflict.
beyond_ai.angle: Intel's capital raise is a useful data point on how tech companies are financing their next moves right now — worth flagging if a client's roadmap depends on chip supply or capex timing.
beyond_ai.starter: Intel's raising $15B in stock right now — anyone else reading that as a sign of how tight capital is getting across the chip industry?

beyond_ai.body: Bristol Myers Squibb will build a $2.3B drug manufacturing campus in Houston, creating roughly 500 permanent jobs.
beyond_ai.angle: A concrete example of pharma reshoring manufacturing capacity to the US — relevant if you're advising clients in life sciences or industrial site selection.
beyond_ai.starter: BMS just committed $2.3B to a new Houston plant — are we seeing more clients bring manufacturing back onshore, or is this still the exception?

beyond_ai.body: Taylor Farms recalled prepared foods containing jalapeños over a salmonella outbreak that has sickened more than 345 people across 27 states, hospitalizing 36.
beyond_ai.angle: A live case study in supply chain and food-safety risk — useful if you're working with clients in retail, food service, or CPG on traceability and recall response.
beyond_ai.starter: 345 people sick across 27 states from one jalapeño recall — how confident are our retail or food clients in their own traceability if something like this hit them?

beyond_ai.body: Jury selection began in the murder trial of Duane "Keefe D" Davis, charged in Tupac Shakur's 1996 killing — nearly three decades after the shooting, and after Davis previously accused Sean "Diddy" Combs of commissioning it (Combs denies).
beyond_ai.angle: No direct relevance to your work, general awareness only.
beyond_ai.starter: The Tupac murder trial is finally starting almost 30 years later — anyone else surprised it took this long to get to court?
